items.actual_relevant_use_quote:
Use the connected strict subextremal parameter domain
$\mathcal P:=\{(m,a,q)\in\mathbb R^3:m>0,\ m^2>a^2+q^2\},$
with its physical Kerr–Newman family and SI conversion as in [[pthm-tgr-kn-family-mechanics]]. Fix positive constants $G_N$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $c$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and $k_B$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Write $E_{\rm par}:\mathcal P\to\mathrm J$, $A_H:\mathcal P\to\mathrm{m^2}$, $J_{\rm SI}:\mathcal P\to\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$, $Q_e:\mathcal P\to\mathrm C$, $\Omega_{\rm SI}:\mathcal P\to\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, and $\Phi_{\rm SI}:\mathcal P\to\mathrm V$ for the smooth parameter functions supplied by [[pthm-tgr-kn-family-mechanics]].

Define the work-subtracted reversible heat one-form on $\mathcal P$ by
$$\delta Q_{\rm rev}:=dE_{\rm par}-\Omega_{\rm SI}\,dJ_{\rm SI}-\Phi_{\rm SI}\,dQ_e.$$
Here a one-form assigns a linear functional to each tangent direction in the family parameter domain; each term has units of joules. Let $S_H:\mathcal P\to\mathbb R$ be a $C^1$ function with values measured in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. It is a state function here in the explicit sense that its value is assigned to each family parameter point and does not depend on a path used to reach that point.

Assume the mathematical premise $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] required by the selected spectral supplier. This is not a physical postulate.

Let $\kappa_{\rm geom}>0$, in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, be the geometric coefficient $\nabla_\chi\chi=\kappa_{\rm geom}\chi$ for the same selected generator $\chi$ and reference normalization used in the physical family, as defined conditionally in [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Identify the inverse-length parameter $\kappa$ of the reduced exponential-current branch in [[pthm-tgr-reduced-horizon-temperature]] with this $\kappa_{\rm geom}$. Adopt the additional reference-temperature identification $T_K:=T_{\rm red}$, where $T_{\rm red}$ is that supplier's effective reference temperature. In this postulate $T_K$ names only the selected reference scale in the reversible relation; it is not a local proper-temperature field and does not assert a stationary bath, a KMS state, or an observed detector reading.

Adopt the reversible thermodynamic identification
$$\delta Q_{\rm rev}=T_K\,dS_H$$
throughout this selected family. This physical identification is an additional assumption. The geometric family identity and the reduced effective-temperature model do not by themselves assert it. No global entropy zero or identification with a quantum-gravity microstate count or an unrenormalized outside-state entropy is adopted.
items.finding: Adopts work-subtracted deltaQ=dEpar-OmegaSI dJ-PhiSI dQ on the full strict subextremal P, retaining both work terms. Entropy is a separate C1 state function and reference-temperature equality is an explicit additional adoption for the same specified horizon generator. Same positive kappa normalization is used; no fixeda no-work inference, arbitrary bath, KMS or empirical claim.

actual_proof_quotes.1.1:
Under the mathematical premise [A2], by [F2], the work-subtracted one-form $\delta Q_{\rm rev}$ defined in [A1] is exactly $\frac{\kappa_{\rm acc}c^2}{8\pi G_N}dA_H$: the angular-momentum and electric-charge work terms cancel with the same terms in its definition. The physical postulate [A1] identifies this same one-form with $T_K\,dS_H$. Hence
$$T_K\,dS_H=\frac{\kappa_{\rm acc}c^2}{8\pi G_N}\,dA_H.$$
This is conditional on the selected stationary-family and thermodynamic assumptions. [given, A2, F2, A1, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.1.2: Under [A2], by [L1] and the explicit generator identification in [A1], $T_K=T_{\rm red}=\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}/(2\pi k_B)$. By [F1], this equals $\hbar\kappa_{\rm acc}/(2\pi c k_B)>0$; the strict subextremal hypothesis is what permits division by this temperature. [given, A2, F1, L1, A1, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.2.1:
Divide the equality in step 1.1 by the positive temperature in step 1.2 and use [F1]:
$$dS_H=\frac{c^2\kappa_{\rm acc}}{8\pi G_N}\frac{2\pi c k_B}{\hbar\kappa_{\rm acc}}\,dA_H=\frac{k_Bc^3}{4G_N\hbar}\,dA_H=\frac{k_B}{4\ell_P^2}\,dA_H.$$
The coefficient has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$, so the right-hand side has entropy units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.3.1:
For arbitrary $x_0=(m_0,a_0,q_0)$ and $x_1=(m_1,a_1,q_1)$ in $\mathcal P$, put $v_i=(a_i,q_i)$ with its Euclidean norm and let $\gamma(t)=(1-t)x_0+tx_1$ for $0\le t\le1$. Since $m_i>\|v_i\|_2$, for every such $t$,
$$m(t)=(1-t)m_0+tm_1>(1-t)\|v_0\|_2+t\|v_1\|_2\ge\|(1-t)v_0+tv_1\|_2=\sqrt{a(t)^2+q(t)^2}.$$
Thus the segment stays in $\mathcal P$. Set $R:=S_H-\frac{k_B}{4\ell_P^2}A_H$; step 2.1 gives $dR=0$. The path $\gamma$ is smooth; since $\mathcal P$ is open, it maps a neighborhood of every $t\in(0,1)$ into $\mathcal P$. The chain rule [F5] gives $(R\circ\gamma)'(t)=dR_{\gamma(t)}(x_1-x_0)=0$. Also $R\circ\gamma$ is continuous on $[0,1]$ and differentiable on $(0,1)$, so [F6] yields $R(x_1)=R(x_0)$. [F3, step 2.1, F5, F6, construct]
actual_proof_quotes.4.1: Since $x_0,x_1$ were arbitrary, $R$ has one constant value $s_*$ on the connected family $\mathcal P$, proving the displayed formula. No reference value of $S_H$ was adopted; adding any constant to it leaves [A1] unchanged, in accord with the mathematical calibration freedom [F4]. This fixes the conditional area coefficient but not an entropy zero. [A1, F4, step 3.1] ∎

actual_proof_quotes.1.1:
Under [A2], for either mass $m_*>0$, set $J_{\rm SI}=Q_e=0$. The map in [F1] gives $a=q=0$ and $m=G_Nm_*/c^2>0$; hence $s=m$, $r_+=2m$, and $D=4m^2$. Therefore
$$A_H(m_*)=4\pi D=16\pi m^2=\frac{16\pi G_N^2m_*^2}{c^4}.$$
This is the selected stationary-family area, not a process or observation. [given, F1, A1, A2, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.1.2:
Under [A2], apply [F2] at both states in [A1]. The same constant $s_*$ cancels, giving
$$S_H(m_{*,2})-S_H(m_{*,1})=\frac{k_B}{4\ell_P^2}\left(A_H(m_{*,2})-A_H(m_{*,1})\right).$$
[F2, A1, A2, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.2.1: Substitute the two areas from step 1.1 into step 1.2 and use $\ell_P^2=G_N\hbar/c^3$. The coefficient simplifies to $4\pi k_BG_N/(\hbar c)$, which has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,kg^{-2}}$ before multiplication by the squared-mass difference; the result has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and vanishes when $m_{*,1}=m_{*,2}$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F2, A1, A2, algebra] ∎
